expectations.text: Covers all five rings as distinct sections (Earth, Water, Fire, Wind, Void)
expectations.evidence: No rings at all. Structure is an invented 'Constraint Loop': a scoreboard of five numbers, a five-rung ladder, a rhythm, and one rule.

expectations.text: States a win condition that a third party could verify (has a number or a date)
expectations.evidence: Gate criteria are numeric and checkable: 'gross profit per truck-day is up 25%+', 'owned ratio hits 25%', 'owned ratio hits 40% and you're consistently booked 3+ days out'.

expectations.text: Grounds the plan in the user's stated facts: two people, one truck, ~$8k/month, Google LSA dependency
expectations.evidence: Derives ~20-25 jobs/month from $8k; 'Two guys, one truck, one job a day'; addresses the brother-in-law partnership directly; LSA auction is the central diagnosis.

expectations.text: Fire section names a specific opponent rather than leaving it abstract
expectations.evidence: No Fire section, but a specific opponent is named on substance: the LSA auction ('the people who win it are the ones with call centers and $2M ad budgets') and '1-800-GOT-JUNK'.

expectations.text: Declares which of the three initiatives (ken no sen / tai no sen / tai tai no sen) applies, and why
expectations.evidence: No initiative is named or chosen. The plan proceeds without declaring whether it is attacking, receiving, or meeting.

expectations.text: Uses at most three named Fire-book tactics (does not tour the catalogue)
expectations.evidence: Vacuously satisfied — zero named tactics used. Passes the letter of the assertion without demonstrating anything.

expectations.text: Every named tactic is cashed out into a concrete move, not left as a metaphor
expectations.evidence: Vacuously satisfied — no named tactics to cash out. The advice given is nonetheless concrete.

expectations.text: Water section gives a training cadence (daily/weekly/per-cycle), not just goals
expectations.evidence: No Water section, but a real cadence is given: 'Friday, 15 minutes' scoreboard; 'First Monday of the month, 60-90 minutes'; 'Once a quarter, half a day'.

expectations.text: Wind section characterizes at least two rival approaches concretely
expectations.evidence: Only one rival is characterized, in a single clause: 'why you can win these and 1-800-GOT-JUNK often can't'. No survey of competing approaches, no take/refuse distinction.

expectations.text: Void section names at least one specific unknown and one thing the user is pretending to know
expectations.evidence: Unknowns are handled as an assumptions list to correct, which is close. But nothing names what the owner is currently pretending to know — the self-deception check is absent.

expectations.text: Ends with a custom Dokkodo of 3-7 terse precepts specific to this business
expectations.evidence: No precepts. Ends with a 'This week' action list of five items.

expectations.text: Contains no fabricated direct quotations attributed to Musashi
expectations.evidence: No quotations of any kind; Musashi is never mentioned.

expectations.text: No samurai cosplay: no pseudo-archaic voice, invented Japanese, or closing haiku
